one_liner: Senior team-lead contracting officer role at DISA, Fort Meade: leading contract specialists through solicitations, negotiations, awards and administration of IT contracts.
fit_summary: This GS-14 requires a year of GS-13-equivalent contracting experience: planning acquisitions, soliciting, evaluating, negotiating and administering contracts. Daniel's consulting work at IEM may have touched government contracts, but nothing on file shows hands-on contracting at that level. Daniel's policy knowledge and people skills don't substitute for it.
eligibility: Open to the public under DoD Direct Hire Authority (5 USC 9905); veterans' preference does not apply.
Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution is required for the 1102 series (the pre-2000 exemption won't apply to you).

One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-13: planning acquisitions, writing acquisition documents, and soliciting, evaluating, negotiating and administering contracts. Education cannot substitute.
Must be able to obtain a Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance.
Apply by emailing your resume to disa.meade.psd.mbx.pla-1102-applications@mail.mil, referencing "Announcement 13069410".
strategy: Before applying, honestly inventory your IEM work: list any proposals, task orders, contract modifications, deliverables or negotiations you handled. Apply only if you can document a year of GS-13-level contracting work.

If your IEM role was contractor-side capture, proposal or contract management, frame it as working under FAR-based government contracts. Be clear that you were on the contractor side, not the government side.
State the specialized experience explicitly in the resume body, which the posting requires. Keep it within two pages with dates and hours per week.

If you're not qualified, target entry or developmental 1102 roles instead: GS-7/9 contract specialist positions, DoD acquisition intern programs, or Pathways. Those can lead to this level within a few years.
Leverage your relationship skills by emphasizing 'mission partner' engagement and communication, which are listed competencies.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client] contract [number/type] at IEM by [preparing deliverables/managing modifications/tracking performance] for a [$ value] [emergency management/recovery] program, [hours/week].
Coordinated with [client program managers/contracting officers] on [scope, schedule, funding] for [number] task orders, ensuring compliance with [FAR/contract terms].
Led a team of [number] staff to deliver [work product] by [deadline], assigning tasks and tracking work plans.
interview_questions: Walk us through a complex acquisition you planned from requirement through award.
How have you led a team of contract specialists under competing deadlines?
Describe a negotiation with a contractor and how you reached a fair and reasonable price.
How do you assess contractor performance and handle a non-performing contractor?
watch_outs: Specialized experience is strict and can't be waived or substituted with education. Overstating qualifications can get you removed from consideration.
A bachelor's degree is mandatory; confirm you have one from an accredited school.
SCI clearance is required, which means a lengthy background investigation.
Fort Meade is a long commute from Manassas; telework is available but the job is not remote.
